supported: HWP5/HWPX footnote paragraphs in body, table-cell and textbox stories support exact owner-addressed selection, navigation, plain-text insertion/deletion, paragraph splitting/merging where representable, Undo/Redo and safe save. Note type, anchor section/paragraph/control, owner path, instance ID, number, inner paragraph and run/paragraph metadata remain bound to the same footnote.
refused: Endnotes remain P5-R-EN. Unsupported note structures, ambiguous/stale owners, body-address aliases, cross-note edits, unsupported paragraph metadata and non-plain-text mutations fail closed without partial changes.
preservation: The session and RHWP APIs resolve a note through its exact story owner path, anchor control, note type, instance ID, number and inner paragraph; note addresses do not alias body, table, textbox or another note.

HWP5 T009 preserves the complete decompressed DocInfo stream and CFB stream inventory. Independent record comparison found only the owned note PARA_HEADER length and PARA_TEXT records changed in BodyText/Section0; note identity and other notes remained unchanged.

HWPX T009 preserves OPC inventory and all unrelated parts. Only Contents/section0.xml and the two known preview parts changed; Preview/PrvText.txt was the exact content-independent CRLF placeholder, and Preview/PrvImage.png passed PNG chunk CRC and source-dimension checks (724x1024).

The note-specific rendered crop, centered on the independently resolved cursor rectangle, matched byte-for-byte after same-session reopen and fresh-process reopen for each fixture. The full HWP page is reflowed after reopening; paragraph text/control state is independently unchanged and the saved note crop/position is stable.
Undo and Redo restored the original and edited canvas hashes. Native tests used trusted X11 pointer and keyboard events; saves reported saved, synced=true, changedSince=false and empty findings.
Unknown, unsupported or ambiguous note mutations remain fail-closed. Rejected operations do not partially mutate the document or history.
